paragraphs.title: The plague of frogs comes upon Egypt

easy.question: Whom did the LORD tell Moses to speak to?
answers: Aaron
Pharaoh
The magicians
easy.explanation: The LORD told Moses, “Say to Aaron.”

easy.question: What was Aaron commanded to use?
answers: A jar
His staff
A net
easy.explanation: Aaron was commanded to stretch out his hand with his staff.

easy.question: What came up and covered the land of Egypt?
answers: Blood
Darkness
Frogs
easy.explanation: The frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

medium.question: What did Aaron do after he was commanded to stretch out his hand?
answers: He stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt
He went to Pharaoh
He gathered the magicians
medium.explanation: Aaron obeyed the command and stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt.

medium.question: In the phrase “over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds,” what are the ponds?
answers: Pools or bodies of water
Royal palaces
Dry fields
medium.explanation: The ponds are listed alongside streams and rivers, so they are bodies of water.

medium.question: What did the magicians do after the frogs came up?
answers: They returned the frogs to the water
They did the same with their enchantments and brought up frogs too
They fled from Egypt
medium.explanation: The verse says that the magicians did the same with their enchantments and brought frogs upon Egypt.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the frogs coming up from all the waters of Egypt?
answers: The plague was limited to one place
The plague spread throughout the land
The plague affected only the magicians
challenge.explanation: The command included streams, rivers, and ponds, and the frogs covered the land; the plague was therefore widespread.

challenge.question: What does the statement “the magicians did so” show about their action?
answers: They imitated the bringing up of the frogs
They ended the plague
They prevented Aaron from acting
challenge.explanation: The magicians performed a similar action and brought up frogs as well.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the action followed an orderly command?
answers: The LORD commanded Moses, Moses told Aaron, and Aaron carried it out
The magicians acted first, and only afterward did the LORD speak
Aaron acted without receiving instructions
challenge.explanation: The order is: the LORD commands Moses, Moses commands Aaron, and Aaron acts.

questions.question: What can we infer from the frogs coming up from all the waters of Egypt?
answers: The plague was limited to one place
The plague spread throughout the land
The plague affected only the magicians
questions.explanation: The command included streams, rivers, and ponds, and the frogs covered the land; the plague was therefore widespread.

questions.question: What does the statement “the magicians did so” show about their action?
answers: They imitated the bringing up of the frogs
They ended the plague
They prevented Aaron from acting
questions.explanation: The magicians performed a similar action and brought up frogs as well.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the action followed an orderly command?
answers: The LORD commanded Moses, Moses told Aaron, and Aaron carried it out
The magicians acted first, and only afterward did the LORD speak
Aaron acted without receiving instructions
questions.explanation: The order is: the LORD commands Moses, Moses commands Aaron, and Aaron acts.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh asks for the frogs to be removed

easy.question: Who called Moses and Aaron and asked them to pray?
answers: Pharaoh
The people
Joshua
easy.explanation: Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and asked them to entreat the LORD.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh promise would happen after the frogs were removed?
answers: The frogs would remain in the river
The people would be sent to worship the LORD
Moses would remain in the palace
easy.explanation: Pharaoh said, “I will let the people go, that they may do sacrifice unto the LORD.”

easy.question: Where would the frogs remain after they were removed?
answers: In the houses
In the fields
In the river
easy.explanation: Moses said that the frogs would remain only in the river.

medium.question: What did Moses ask Pharaoh to set so that he could pray for the frogs to be removed?
answers: The day when the frogs would be removed
The place where the people would gather
The number of frogs
medium.explanation: Moses asked Pharaoh, “When shall I intreat for thee?”—that is, when he wanted the plague removed.

medium.question: What did Moses say would happen “to morrow”?
answers: The frogs would multiply
The frogs would be removed
The people would return to Egypt
medium.explanation: Moses said that the frogs would depart from Pharaoh, his houses, servants, and people the next day.

medium.question: What happened after the frogs died?
answers: They were gathered into heaps, and the land stank
They returned to the houses
They vanished without a trace
medium.explanation: The frogs were gathered into heaps, and the land stank because of them.

challenge.question: Why did Moses let Pharaoh choose the time for the frogs to be removed?
answers: To show that the removal would happen at the time Pharaoh chose, not by chance
To give the frogs time to multiply
To delay his prayer to the LORD
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh’s choice showed that the LORD could remove the plague exactly when Moses announced, proving that there was none like the LORD.

challenge.question: What does the statement “they shall remain in the river only” show?
answers: The plague would continue at the same strength
The river would remain a natural home for the frogs, while the houses would be cleared
Pharaoh had not really asked for the plague to be removed
challenge.explanation: Leaving the frogs only in the river distinguished their natural habitat from the homes and surroundings of the people.

challenge.question: What caused Pharaoh to harden his heart again?
answers: The frogs multiplied after the prayer
Moses and Aaron did not leave Egypt
When he saw that there was relief, he stopped listening to them
challenge.explanation: After the plague was removed and there was relief, Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not keep his promise to let the people go.

questions.question: Why did Moses let Pharaoh choose the time for the frogs to be removed?
answers: To show that the removal would happen at the time Pharaoh chose, not by chance
To give the frogs time to multiply
To delay his prayer to the LORD
questions.explanation: Pharaoh’s choice showed that the LORD could remove the plague exactly when Moses announced, proving that there was none like the LORD.

questions.question: What does the statement “they shall remain in the river only” show?
answers: The plague would continue at the same strength
The river would remain a natural home for the frogs, while the houses would be cleared
Pharaoh had not really asked for the plague to be removed
questions.explanation: Leaving the frogs only in the river distinguished their natural habitat from the homes and surroundings of the people.

questions.question: What caused Pharaoh to harden his heart again?
answers: The frogs multiplied after the prayer
Moses and Aaron did not leave Egypt
When he saw that there was relief, he stopped listening to them
questions.explanation: After the plague was removed and there was relief, Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not keep his promise to let the people go.

paragraphs.title: The plague of lice from the dust of the land

easy.question: Whom did the LORD tell Moses to command to strike the dust of the land?
answers: Aaron
Pharaoh
The magicians
easy.explanation: The LORD told Moses to tell Aaron to strike the dust of the land with his staff.

easy.question: What did the dust of the land become after Aaron struck it?
answers: Blood
Lice
Frogs
easy.explanation: After Aaron struck the dust, it became lice throughout Egypt.

easy.question: Who had the lice?
answers: Only Pharaoh
Only the livestock
People and animals
easy.explanation: The verse says that the lice were upon both people and animals.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Aaron struck the dust, and the lice appeared
Pharaoh listened to the magicians, and then the lice disappeared
The magicians brought out the lice, and then Aaron struck the dust
medium.explanation: First Aaron struck the dust of the land, and afterward the lice appeared.

medium.question: What did the magicians try to do after the lice appeared?
answers: Turn the lice into frogs
Bring out lice with their enchantments
Warn the Israelites
medium.explanation: The magicians tried to bring out lice by their enchantments, but they could not.

medium.question: What does the verse say happened when the magicians tried to reproduce the plague?
answers: They succeeded completely
They could not do it, while lice remained on people and animals
They made the lice disappear
medium.explanation: The magicians tried to bring forth lice but could not; the lice remained on people and animals.

challenge.question: Why did the magicians say to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God”?
answers: They could not produce or remove the lice
They wanted to punish Pharaoh
They thought the lice came from the river
challenge.explanation: The magicians could not reproduce the plague, so they recognized that it involved divine power.

challenge.question: What contrast is shown between the magicians’ response and Pharaoh’s response?
answers: The magicians rejoiced, while Pharaoh was afraid
The magicians recognized God’s power, while Pharaoh hardened his heart
The magicians fled, while Pharaoh removed the lice
challenge.explanation: The magicians said that the plague was the finger of God, but Pharaoh did not listen and continued to harden his heart.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the repeated statement that the lice were “throughout all the land of Egypt”?
answers: The lice were only near Pharaoh’s palace
The lice appeared only among wealthy Egyptians
The plague was widespread throughout Egypt
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes that the plague was not local but affected the whole land of Egypt.

questions.question: Why did the magicians say to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God”?
answers: They could not produce or remove the lice
They wanted to punish Pharaoh
They thought the lice came from the river
questions.explanation: The magicians could not reproduce the plague, so they recognized that it involved divine power.

questions.question: What contrast is shown between the magicians’ response and Pharaoh’s response?
answers: The magicians rejoiced, while Pharaoh was afraid
The magicians recognized God’s power, while Pharaoh hardened his heart
The magicians fled, while Pharaoh removed the lice
questions.explanation: The magicians said that the plague was the finger of God, but Pharaoh did not listen and continued to harden his heart.

questions.question: What can we infer from the repeated statement that the lice were “throughout all the land of Egypt”?
answers: The lice were only near Pharaoh’s palace
The lice appeared only among wealthy Egyptians
The plague was widespread throughout Egypt
questions.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes that the plague was not local but affected the whole land of Egypt.

paragraphs.title: Warning of the plague of flies and the distinction between Israel and Egypt

easy.question: Who commanded Moses to stand before Pharaoh?
answers: The LORD
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The LORD told Moses to rise early and stand before Pharaoh.

easy.question: Where would Moses find Pharaoh in the morning?
answers: In the palace
By the water
In the land of Goshen
easy.explanation: The verse says that Pharaoh would come out to the water.

easy.question: Which plague was about to come upon Egypt?
answers: Hail
Darkness
Flies
easy.explanation: The LORD warned that He would send swarms of flies upon Egypt if Pharaoh did not let the people go.

medium.question: What would happen if Pharaoh did not let the Israelites go?
answers: Swarms of flies would be sent upon Egypt
The sea would open
The staff would disappear
medium.explanation: The LORD said that He would send swarms of flies upon Pharaoh, his servants, his people, and their houses.

medium.question: How would the land of Goshen differ from the land of Egypt?
answers: It would always be dark
There would be no swarms of flies there
It would have no houses
medium.explanation: The LORD would distinguish Goshen, where His people lived, so that no swarms of flies would be there.

medium.question: What does the verse mean by “I will put a division between my people and thy people”?
answers: A punishment
A journey
A distinction or separation
medium.explanation: The statement means that the LORD would separate Israel from Egypt by keeping the flies out of Goshen.

challenge.question: What explicit purpose was given for keeping the flies out of Goshen?
answers: So Pharaoh would know that the LORD was present in the land
So the Israelites could leave immediately
So the Egyptians would move to Goshen
challenge.explanation: The distinction between Goshen and Egypt was meant to show Pharaoh that the LORD was working in the land.

challenge.question: Which detail expands the description of the plague beyond the houses?
answers: The flies would reach only the palace
The ground where the Egyptians lived would also be filled with flies
The flies would appear only at night
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the flies would fill not only the Egyptian houses but also the ground where the Egyptians lived.

challenge.question: Why is the distinction between Goshen and Egypt said to occur “to morrow”?
answers: Moses had not yet arrived in Egypt
Pharaoh asked to delay the plague
It would be a sign taking place on the following day
challenge.explanation: The sign would occur the next day, making the distinction a clear demonstration of the LORD’s action.

questions.question: What explicit purpose was given for keeping the flies out of Goshen?
answers: So Pharaoh would know that the LORD was present in the land
So the Israelites could leave immediately
So the Egyptians would move to Goshen
questions.explanation: The distinction between Goshen and Egypt was meant to show Pharaoh that the LORD was working in the land.

questions.question: Which detail expands the description of the plague beyond the houses?
answers: The flies would reach only the palace
The ground where the Egyptians lived would also be filled with flies
The flies would appear only at night
questions.explanation: The verse says that the flies would fill not only the Egyptian houses but also the ground where the Egyptians lived.

questions.question: Why is the distinction between Goshen and Egypt said to occur “to morrow”?
answers: Moses had not yet arrived in Egypt
Pharaoh asked to delay the plague
It would be a sign taking place on the following day
questions.explanation: The sign would occur the next day, making the distinction a clear demonstration of the LORD’s action.

paragraphs.title: The flies devastate the land of Egypt

easy.question: Who caused the swarms of flies to come upon Egypt?
answers: Pharaoh
The LORD
Pharaoh’s servants
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the LORD did so,” meaning that He brought the swarms of flies.

easy.question: Where did the grievous swarm of flies come?
answers: Only in the wilderness
Only into Pharaoh’s house
Into Pharaoh’s house and the houses of his servants
easy.explanation: The swarm came into Pharaoh’s house and the houses of his servants.

easy.question: What happened to the land of Egypt because of the flies?
answers: The land was corrupted
The land was built up
The land dried out
easy.explanation: The verse says that the land was corrupted because of the swarm of flies.

medium.question: What caused the land of Egypt to be corrupted?
answers: The swarm of flies
Construction
Drought
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the land was corrupted because of the swarm of flies.

medium.question: What happened to the land when the swarm of flies came?
answers: It became beautiful
It was damaged and ruined
It grew larger
medium.explanation: The swarm caused damage and ruin throughout the land.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: The land was corrupted, and then the LORD acted
Pharaoh’s servants drove away the flies, and then the land was corrupted
The LORD acted, the flies came, and the land was corrupted
medium.explanation: First the LORD acted, then the swarm came, and finally the land was corrupted.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the phrase “into Pharaoh’s house, and into his servants’ houses”?
answers: The plague reached both the ruler and his officials
Only Pharaoh’s house was affected
Pharaoh’s servants were not in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both Pharaoh’s house and his servants’ houses, showing that the plague was not limited to one person.

challenge.question: What does the description “a grievous swarm of flies” emphasize?
answers: That the flies were made of metal
That the swarm was especially large or severe
That the flies came only at night
challenge.explanation: “Grievous” describes the swarm’s severity or abundance, not its physical weight.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the damage was widespread rather than local?
answers: The mention of Pharaoh’s house alone
The word “so”
The phrase “into all the land of Egypt”
challenge.explanation: The phrase “into all the land of Egypt” extends the description beyond one house or small area.

questions.question: What can we infer from the phrase “into Pharaoh’s house, and into his servants’ houses”?
answers: The plague reached both the ruler and his officials
Only Pharaoh’s house was affected
Pharaoh’s servants were not in Egypt
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both Pharaoh’s house and his servants’ houses, showing that the plague was not limited to one person.

questions.question: What does the description “a grievous swarm of flies” emphasize?
answers: That the flies were made of metal
That the swarm was especially large or severe
That the flies came only at night
questions.explanation: “Grievous” describes the swarm’s severity or abundance, not its physical weight.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the damage was widespread rather than local?
answers: The mention of Pharaoh’s house alone
The word “so”
The phrase “into all the land of Egypt”
questions.explanation: The phrase “into all the land of Egypt” extends the description beyond one house or small area.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh offers a compromise about the people’s worship

easy.question: Who called for Moses and Aaron?
answers: Pharaoh
The Israelites
The king of Midian
easy.explanation: The verse says that Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh suggest Moses and Aaron do?
answers: Leave Egypt immediately
Sacrifice to their God in the land
Stop praying
easy.explanation: Pharaoh told them, “Go ye, sacrifice to your God in the land.”

easy.question: What did Moses say would happen after he prayed to the LORD?
answers: The Israelites would return to Egypt
Pharaoh would go into the wilderness
The flies would depart from Pharaoh, his servants, and his people
easy.explanation: Moses said that the flies would depart from Pharaoh, his servants, and his people the next day.

medium.question: Why did Moses refuse to have the Israelites sacrifice to the LORD within Egypt?
answers: The Egyptians might stone them
They had no time
Moses did not want to sacrifice
medium.explanation: Moses explained that Israel’s sacrifice was an abomination to the Egyptians, who might stone them if they saw it.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence of events?
answers: Moses prayed, Pharaoh made his offer, and the flies came
Pharaoh agreed to let the people go, Moses went out to pray, and the flies departed
The flies departed, Moses refused to pray, and Pharaoh made his offer
medium.explanation: First Pharaoh agreed to let the people go, then Moses went out to pray, and the flies were to depart.

medium.question: What did Moses mean when he asked Pharaoh not to “mock” him?
answers: Pharaoh should stop speaking with Moses
Pharaoh should not go back on his promise to let the people go
Pharaoh should stop asking for prayer
medium.explanation: Moses warned Pharaoh not to pretend to agree and then withdraw his promise to let the people go.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Moses’ demand to go “three days’ journey into the wilderness”?
answers: He rejected Pharaoh’s offer to sacrifice within Egypt
He intended to remain in Egypt
He asked Pharaoh to go with them
challenge.explanation: Moses emphasized that worship would take place in the wilderness, away from Egypt and its danger.

challenge.question: What was the significance of Moses saying that the sacrifice would be made “before their eyes”?
answers: The Egyptians wanted to join the sacrifice
There was no need to travel far
A public sacrifice could cause the Egyptians to attack the Israelites
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Egyptians would see the sacrifice and might stone the Israelites because they considered it an abomination.

challenge.question: Why did Moses explain that Israel could not sacrifice in front of the Egyptians?
answers: The Egyptians wanted to participate
The Israelites did not need to leave Egypt
The Egyptians might stone them because they considered the sacrifice an abomination
challenge.explanation: Moses said that the Egyptians might attack the Israelites if they saw them performing the sacrifice.

questions.question: What can we infer from Moses’ demand to go “three days’ journey into the wilderness”?
answers: He rejected Pharaoh’s offer to sacrifice within Egypt
He intended to remain in Egypt
He asked Pharaoh to go with them
questions.explanation: Moses emphasized that worship would take place in the wilderness, away from Egypt and its danger.

questions.question: What was the significance of Moses saying that the sacrifice would be made “before their eyes”?
answers: The Egyptians wanted to join the sacrifice
There was no need to travel far
A public sacrifice could cause the Egyptians to attack the Israelites
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Egyptians would see the sacrifice and might stone the Israelites because they considered it an abomination.

questions.question: Why did Moses explain that Israel could not sacrifice in front of the Egyptians?
answers: The Egyptians wanted to participate
The Israelites did not need to leave Egypt
The Egyptians might stone them because they considered the sacrifice an abomination
questions.explanation: Moses said that the Egyptians might attack the Israelites if they saw them performing the sacrifice.

paragraphs.title: The flies depart, but Pharaoh refuses to let the people go

easy.question: Who went out from Pharaoh?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh,” with Moses then praying to the LORD.

easy.question: To whom did Moses pray?
answers: Pharaoh
The LORD
The people
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses entreated the LORD.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh do after the flies were removed?
answers: He let the people go
He prayed to the LORD
He did not let the people go
easy.explanation: Although the flies were removed, Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not let the people go.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence of events?
answers: Moses prayed, the LORD removed the flies, and Pharaoh hardened his heart
Pharaoh let the people go, Moses prayed, and the flies came
The flies remained, Pharaoh prayed, and Moses went out
medium.explanation: First Moses prayed, then the LORD removed the flies, and finally Pharaoh hardened his heart.

medium.question: What did Moses do when he entreated the LORD?
answers: He left quickly
He prayed and pleaded
He became very angry
medium.explanation: Moses turned to the LORD in prayer and earnest supplication.

medium.question: What happened as a result of Moses’ prayer?
answers: Pharaoh immediately let the people go
The flies multiplied throughout the land
The LORD removed the flies
medium.explanation: The LORD did according to Moses’ word and removed the flies from Pharaoh, his servants, and his people.

challenge.question: What does “there remained not one” refer to?
answers: The flies
Pharaoh’s servants
The Israelites
challenge.explanation: The statement follows the description of the flies’ removal, so it means that not one fly remained.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast between the LORD’s actions and Pharaoh’s actions?
answers: The LORD hardened His heart, while Pharaoh removed the flies
The LORD answered Moses’ prayer, but Pharaoh did not change his decision
The LORD refused to help, but Pharaoh let the people go
challenge.explanation: The LORD removed the flies in response to Moses, while Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not let the people go.

challenge.question: What do the words “this time also” show?
answers: This was the first time Pharaoh hardened his heart
Pharaoh had already let the people go
Pharaoh again refused to yield and let the people go
challenge.explanation: The wording shows that Pharaoh repeated his hard-hearted refusal, as he had done before.

questions.question: What does “there remained not one” refer to?
answers: The flies
Pharaoh’s servants
The Israelites
questions.explanation: The statement follows the description of the flies’ removal, so it means that not one fly remained.

questions.question: What is the main contrast between the LORD’s actions and Pharaoh’s actions?
answers: The LORD hardened His heart, while Pharaoh removed the flies
The LORD answered Moses’ prayer, but Pharaoh did not change his decision
The LORD refused to help, but Pharaoh let the people go
questions.explanation: The LORD removed the flies in response to Moses, while Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not let the people go.

questions.question: What do the words “this time also” show?
answers: This was the first time Pharaoh hardened his heart
Pharaoh had already let the people go
Pharaoh again refused to yield and let the people go
questions.explanation: The wording shows that Pharaoh repeated his hard-hearted refusal, as he had done before.
